title: Virtual media and devices
body:
The Media Manager controls bounded in-memory storage, with no host filesystem access. A cassette/file is a name and ordered typed records. One PRINT# writes one record; INPUT# must match its field count and scalar types. Numbers and strings are preserved independently of screen formatting.

Record, rewind, read

  1. Choose a new name and Create & record. This inserts cassette unit -1 in output mode.
  2. Run a TRS program containing PRINT#-1,42,"HELLO".
  3. At INPUT or STOP, choose Rewind to start. The inserted cassette is now input mode at record zero.
  4. Read it using INPUT#-1,N,S$.
  5. Export all media before closing or refreshing the page.

Insert for reading mounts the selected existing file at zero. Rewind operates on the currently inserted tape, which may differ from a highlighted dropdown entry. Unit -2 is available through the standalone device API; the UI manages -1. Wrong mode, missing media, EOF, count/type mismatch and invalid handles produce errors.

Sequential virtual files

10 OPEN "O",1,"notes"
20 PRINT#1,7,"A LOCAL NOTE"
30 CLOSE 1
40 OPEN "I",1,"notes"
50 INPUT#1,N,S$
60 PRINT N;S$
70 CLOSE

Positive handles 1–15 must be opened. Mode O replaces the named virtual file; I requires it to exist. CLOSE with no arguments closes positive handles, not cassette mounts. EOF returns -1 at end. No append mode, random-access records, host paths or URL schemes exist. Comma-separated typed operations are the tested subset, not a disk-byte-format emulator.

Persistence and import

Format retrorealm-basic-devices, version 1, stores named records only. Import validates schema and size before replacement, clears channels/mounts and never runs source. Mount again afterward. A workspace does not contain these records. RUN and program edits keep files; RUN closes positive channels. STOP/CONT preserves live positions. Historical SAVE GAME programs may save only their own variables, not RNG continuation. Portable VM snapshots are not implemented.

Limits and safety

32 named files; 4096 records per file; 256 fields per record; 4096 characters per string; total serialized storage limited to 1048576 JavaScript code units. Names are 1–64 simple ASCII letters/digits/spaces/periods/hyphens/underscores, starting with a letter/digit, with no double dot. Import text is bounded to twice the storage limit and then checked against the actual storage ceiling. Unknown versions, duplicate names, nonfinite values and malformed records are rejected atomically. These are logical JSON images, not CAS/WAV files.
